messages:
From: Sara Jenkins <sara.jenkins@novation.com>

Cc: procurement@novation.com
Date: 2026-11-29T09:14:00-08:00
Subject: Checking options for mid-contract top-up + credits

Hi Mina,

Hope you had a good break. Our usage spiked in October and we're tracking above our renewal baseline — ops is asking whether we can top up capacity mid-contract without waiting for the annual renewal. Two questions: 

1) Can Novation add a mid-term top-up and get pro-rated billing?
2) Are there any temporary credit/discount levers you can offer for the first 90 days (we need runway while we adjust internal load balancing)?

If possible, procurement would like an outline they can share with finance by next Tuesday. Happy to hop on 30 minutes if that's faster.

Thanks,
Sara
Sara Jenkins
Director of AI Platform, Novation Systems
attachments: none
From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
To: Sara Jenkins <sara.jenkins@novation.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-30T11:06:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Checking options for mid-contract top-up + credits

Sara — thanks for the note and congrats on the product momentum. Short answers up front: yes, you can top up mid-contract; and yes, we can structure a short-term credit to smooth the bill for the first 60–90 days. A couple of clarifying points so I scope options properly: 

- Are you looking for a permanent uplift to committed units (annualized) or a temporary burst buffer that sits outside the commit?
- Do you prefer pro-rata invoicing for the top-up month-to-month, or a one-off invoice that gets applied as a credit against the next renewal?

Proposed options I can draft for procurement: 
- Option A — Staged top-up: immediate monthly top-up with 25% credit for first 60 days, then standard rates. Pro-rata monthly invoicing.
- Option B — Bridge voucher: one-time voucher applied as an invoice credit (covers ~30–45 days of incremental usage), top-up converted to annualized commit at renewal if you choose.
- Option C — Temporary burst pool: covered by an elevated burst credit bucket for 90 days, metered usage above commit billed at a discounted overage rate.

I included Ben and Irene to confirm pricing floor and whether legal needs an amendment or a lightweight SOW. If you can confirm which option you prefer I’ll send a draft amendment and an estimated invoice schedule. If easier, let’s do a quick 30-min sync tomorrow.

— Mina
Mina Haddad
Account Manager, Redwood Inference
From: Sara Jenkins <sara.jenkins@novation.com>

Cc: procurement@novation.com
Date: 2026-12-01T08:22:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Checking options for mid-contract top-up + credits

Thanks Mina — good options. Procurement prefers Option B (Bridge voucher applied as a credit) because finance wants a single document to attach to the PO. Two follow-ups: 

- Can the voucher be sized to cover roughly our incremental usage for December–January (we estimate +45% to baseline, attached a short usage extract).
- Procurement will need a DocuSign-ready amendment + a simple invoice estimate by Friday EOD so they can route the PO.

If you can size the voucher and send the amendment, I’ll get procurement to prepare a PO. 30-min call optional — I think we can proceed by email.

Sara

Ben / Irene — Novation (NV-2026-0491) wants Option B (one-time voucher applied as invoice credit). They need: 

- Voucher sized for ~45% incremental usage for Dec–Jan (Sara attached a usage extract).
- DocuSign-ready amendment and an invoice estimate by Friday EOD (they plan to route PO to finance).

I’ve sketched numbers below (ballpark): 
- Estimated incremental tokens = 12M tokens/month over baseline => 24M tokens for two months.
- Proposed voucher cover: 18M tokens (covers ~75% of incremental; balance billed as discounted overage).
- Suggested discount on billed overage: 20% for first 60 days.

Irene — can you confirm the voucher USD value for 18M tokens (use current rate sheet) and whether we should classify this as a credit (applied against next invoice) vs prepayment? Ben — will this require a pricing exception or is it within standard sales ops band?

I’ll attach a draft amendment once I have numbers.
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-12-02T13:47:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Internal: Novation ask — bridge voucher + amendment (PO timeline Friday)

Thanks Mina — we can do this without exec approval. Irene, quick guidance: put voucher value at $11,250 (matches 18M tokens at $0.000625/token on their current tier). Structure: one-line amendment (term: immediate effect, credits to be applied to next invoice; voucher expires 90 days after execution). Overage to be billed at list overage rate less 20% for 60 days, then revert.

Operational notes:
- Finance prefers credit treatment (applied against next invoice) rather than prepayment for our internal recognition.
- Legal usually accepts a short amendment for a voucher; we can include a sentence referencing original agreement SOW and add the voucher appendix.

Mina — I’ll attach a pricing ops stub and will finalize the numbers. Recommended next step: send amendment PDF + DocuSign link to Sara after Irene confirms formal GL coding.
